# 👯 What is KNN?

## The big idea

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.incremental}
- 📌 To predict a new data point, find its **K nearest neighbors** in the training set.
- 🗳️ Let those neighbors **vote** on what label to assign.
- 🎯 That's it. **No model is "trained"** — KNN just memorizes.
- 🤔 *"Show me your friends and I'll tell you who you are."*
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](img/knn.png){fig-align="center"}
:::
:::

::: {.footer}
[Machine Learning Basics with KNN](https://towardsdatascience.com/machine-learning-basics-with-the-k-nearest-neighbors-algorithm-6a6e71d01761)
:::

---

## Visualizing KNN

![](img/knn2.png){fig-align="center" width="65%"}

::: {.fragment}
> The **green dot** wants to be classified. With **K = 3**, it asks the 3 nearest dots — and goes with the majority. ✅
:::

::: {.footer}
[KNN Tutorial — Machine Learning Basics](https://pub.towardsai.net/k-nearest-neighbors-knn-algorithm-tutorial-machine-learning-basics-ml-ec6756d3e0ac)
:::

---

## How does it measure "near"?

**Euclidean distance** — straight-line distance between two points.

![](img/euclidean_rep.png){fig-align="center" width="55%"}

::: {.fragment}
> 📏 In 2D it's the Pythagorean theorem. In *p* dimensions, same idea — just more terms.
:::

::: {.footer}
[Euclidean distance — Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance)
:::

---

## Other distances exist

::: {.callout-note}
## A small zoo of distances 🦒
- **Euclidean** — the default, straight-line.
- **Manhattan** — sum of absolute differences (city-block routes).
- **Minkowski** — generalizes both (parameter `p`).
- **Cosine** — angle between vectors (text + recommender systems).
- **Hamming** — for categorical / string data.
:::

::: {.fragment}
> 🌟 In `tidymodels` you can pick via `dist_power` and `weight_func`. Default Euclidean is usually fine.
:::

# 🎛️ The K parameter

## What does K do?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Small K (e.g. K = 1)**

::: {.incremental}
- Predictions follow every training point exactly. 🌀
- **Low bias, high variance.**
- Prone to **overfitting** — and very sensitive to noise.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Large K (e.g. K = 100)**

::: {.incremental}
- Predictions get **smoothed out**. 🧈
- **High bias, low variance.**
- Risks **underfitting** — and misses local patterns.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
> 🎯 **The right K is somewhere in between.** That's why we tune it with cross-validation.
:::

# ⚖️ Pros & Cons

## What KNN is great at

::: {.incremental}
- 🟢 **Conceptually simple** — easy to explain to non-stats people.
- 🟢 **No model assumptions** — non-parametric.
- 🟢 **Works for both classification and regression.**
- 🟢 **Naturally handles non-linear** decision boundaries.
- 🟢 Famously good in some applications: **genetics**, **text similarity**, **recommender systems**.
:::

---

## Where KNN struggles 😬

::: {.incremental}
- 🔴 **Slow at prediction time** — has to compute distances to *all* training points.
- 🔴 **Bad with high-dimensional data** — the *curse of dimensionality*.
- 🔴 **Very sensitive to feature scale** — must `step_normalize()`.
- 🔴 **Sensitive to imbalanced data** — majority class dominates the votes.
- 🔴 **Sensitive to outliers and irrelevant features.**
:::

::: {.fragment}
> 🌟 **Translation:** KNN needs careful preprocessing. We'll handle scaling and imbalance in the recipe.
:::

# 💻 KNN with `tidymodels`

## Today's task 🎯

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
> **Can KNN predict whether an adolescent has been bullied?** 🧒💔

::: {.incremental}
- **Outcome**: `Bullying` (binary)
- **Predictors**: every other risky-behavior item (after dropping leaky ones)
- **Why KNN?** Last model of the day — and a chance to see how a totally different idea handles the same data.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](https://media.giphy.com/media/iFqLTjlvndks0/giphy.gif){fig-align="center"}
:::
:::

---

## Same 7 steps you've used 5 times 🔁

::: {.incremental}
1. **Split** train / test (with `strata =`)
2. **Resample** with V-fold CV
3. **Recipe** ← extra care for KNN: **scale + impute + downsample**
4. **Spec** ← `nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune())`
5. **Workflow** = recipe + spec
6. **Tune** + sanity-check
7. `finalize_workflow()` → `last_fit()` → metrics
:::

::: {.fragment}
> 🌟 **Sixth time's the charm.** You've got this.
:::

---

## Setup — load packages 📦

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(MLearnYRBSS)
library(themis)        # <- for step_downsample()
library(kknn)
library(janitor)

data("riskyBehaviors")
```

---

## Need to install first? 📦

::: {.callout-note}
## One-time install
```r
pak::pak(c(
    "tidymodels", "kknn", "themis",
    "janitor", "MLearnYRBSS"
))
```
:::

::: {.fragment}
> 🌟 `kknn` is the standard KNN engine for `tidymodels`. `themis` adds resampling steps (like `step_downsample()`) for imbalanced data.
:::

---

## 1️⃣ Recode the outcome

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1-5"
#| output-location: fragment
riskyBehaviors_analysis <-
    riskyBehaviors |>
    mutate(Bullying = factor(Bullying)) |>
    drop_na(Bullying) |>
    select(-c(SourceAlcohol, SourceVaping,
              contains("Times"), contains("Days"),
              CyberBullying))
```

::: {.fragment}
> `0` = not bullied · `1` = has been bullied. We drop **`CyberBullying`** to avoid leakage and the time-frequency items to keep things clean.
:::

# 2️⃣ Split + Resample

## Train / test split — stratified

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1|3-6|8-9|11"
#| output-location: fragment
set.seed(2023)

bullying_split <- initial_split(
    riskyBehaviors_analysis,
    strata = Bullying
)

bullying_train <- training(bullying_split)
bullying_test  <- testing(bullying_split)

bullying_split
```

::: {.fragment}
> 🌟 You know the drill. `strata =` keeps the class balance even.
:::

---

## Sanity check — class balance

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Training**
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
bullying_train |>
    tabyl(Bullying) |>
    adorn_pct_formatting(0) |>
    adorn_totals()
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Testing**
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
bullying_test |>
    tabyl(Bullying) |>
    adorn_pct_formatting(0) |>
    adorn_totals()
```
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-warning}
## 🚨 Class imbalance alert
Notice the **0 / 1 split** is uneven. KNN is *especially* sensitive to this — it will just keep predicting the majority class.
We'll fix it in the recipe with `step_downsample()`. 🛠️
:::
:::

---

## Cross-validation folds

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1|3"
#| output-location: fragment
set.seed(2023)

bullying_folds <- vfold_cv(bullying_train, v = 5, strata = Bullying)
bullying_folds
```

::: {.fragment}
> **5 folds** of the *training* set. Each candidate K will be evaluated on all 5.
:::

# 3️⃣ Recipe + Spec + Workflow

## Recipe — KNN needs special care 🧴

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1-2|3|4|5|6|7|8"
#| output-location: fragment
bullying_recipe <-
    recipe(Bullying ~ ., data = bullying_train) |>
    step_downsample(Bullying, under_ratio = 1) |>
    step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
    step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

bullying_recipe
```

---

## What each step does 🛠️

::: {.callout-tip}
## KNN's special-care kit
- **`step_downsample()`** — randomly drops rows from the majority class to fix imbalance. *(Critical for KNN.)*
- **`step_zv()`** — drops zero-variance predictors (no info, just noise).
- **`step_normalize()`** — *mandatory* for KNN. Without it, predictors with bigger units dominate the distance.
- **`step_impute_*()`** — KNN can't compute distance with `NA`s.
- **`step_dummy()`** — `kknn` needs numeric predictors only.
:::

::: {.fragment}
> 🌟 **Skip `step_normalize()` and your KNN is broken.** Don't ask how I know.
:::

---

## Spec — `kknn` 👯

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1-3|4-5"
#| output-location: fragment
kknn_spec <-
    nearest_neighbor(
        neighbors = tune()    # ⬅️ we'll tune K
    ) |>
    set_mode("classification") |>
    set_engine("kknn")

kknn_spec
```

::: {.fragment}
> Yesterday: `decision_tree(...)`. This morning: `boost_tree(...)`. Now: `nearest_neighbor(...)`. **Same pattern, different model.** ✨
:::

---

## Workflow — bundle it 🔗

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2|3|4"
#| output-location: fragment
kknn_workflow <-
    workflow() |>
    add_recipe(bullying_recipe) |>
    add_model(kknn_spec)

kknn_workflow
```

::: {.fragment}
> Recipe + spec, neatly packaged. **You've done this 5 times now.** 💪
:::

# 4️⃣ Tune K

## Build the tuning grid

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
neighbor_grid <- tibble(neighbors = c(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 15, 21, 31, 51))
neighbor_grid
```

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-tip}
## Why **odd** numbers?
With binary classification + odd K, you can never get a tie vote. 🗳️
:::
:::

---

## Run the tuning ⚙️

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1|3|5-9|11"
#| output-location: fragment
doParallel::registerDoParallel()

set.seed(2023)

knn_tune <- tune_grid(
    kknn_workflow,
    resamples = bullying_folds,
    grid      = neighbor_grid,
    metrics   = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy)
)

doParallel::stopImplicitCluster()
```

::: {.fragment}
> KNN tuning is **fast** — no model is actually trained, just distances are computed. ⚡
:::

---

## Show the best K

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
show_best(knn_tune, metric = "roc_auc")
```

::: {.fragment}
> Top 5 K values, ranked by mean ROC AUC across the 5 folds. 🏆
:::

---

## Visualize the tuning results

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| output-location: slide
autoplot(knn_tune)
```

::: {.fragment}
> 📈 ROC AUC vs K. Look for the **plateau** before performance starts to drop.
:::

---

## Pick the best K

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
best_k <- select_best(knn_tune, metric = "roc_auc")
best_k
```

::: {.fragment}
> One number — our winning K. **Don't commit yet** — let's check it first. 🤔
:::

# 5️⃣ Sanity-Check Before Committing

## How does our chosen K *actually* do? 🔍

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2|3|4"
#| output-location: fragment
kknn_workflow |>
    finalize_workflow(best_k) |>
    fit_resamples(resamples = bullying_folds) |>
    collect_metrics()
```

::: {.fragment}
> An honest, CV-estimated performance for our **single** chosen K.
:::

---

## 🔄 Decision point — last time today!

::: {.incremental}
- 😀 **Metrics look good** → lock it in, evaluate on test. ✅
- 😬 **Metrics look bad** → **STOP**. Re-tune. 🛑
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-warning}
## 🚨 Important
Once you commit with `last_fit()`, **you've used your test set**. No going back.
:::
:::

---

## Looks good? Lock it in 🔒

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
final_wf <- finalize_workflow(kknn_workflow, best_k)

final_wf
```

::: {.fragment}
> Best K plugged in. **Ready for the test set.** ✅
:::

# 6️⃣ Evaluate on the Test Set

## `last_fit()` — for the **6th** time today ✨

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2-6"
#| output-location: fragment
bullying_last_fit <- last_fit(
    final_wf,
    split   = bullying_split,
    metrics = metric_set(accuracy, kap, roc_auc, sensitivity, specificity)
)

bullying_last_fit
```

::: {.fragment}
> Same magic as Lasso, Trees, RF, XGBoost — fits on train, predicts on test, computes metrics honestly. 🪄
:::

---

## Test-set metrics

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
collect_metrics(bullying_last_fit)
```

::: {.fragment}
> Compare to your **CV sanity-check** metrics. Same ballpark = your KNN generalizes. 🎉
:::

---

## Test-set predictions

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
predictions_testing <-
    bullying_last_fit |>
    collect_predictions() |>
    select(-.row, -.config)

predictions_testing
```

---

## Confusion matrix

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| output-location: slide
predictions_testing |>
    conf_mat(truth = Bullying, estimate = .pred_class) |>
    autoplot(type = "heatmap")
```

::: {.fragment}
> Look at the **off-diagonals** — what kind of mistakes is your KNN making?
:::

---

## ROC curve on the test set

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| output-location: slide
predictions_testing |>
    roc_curve(truth = Bullying, .pred_1, event_level = "second") |>
    autoplot()
```

::: {.fragment}
> Top-left corner = good. Diagonal = random guessing. 🎲
:::

---

## Make sure your metrics are *interpretable* 🧠

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: fragment
multi_metric <- metric_set(sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, kap)

multi_metric(
    predictions_testing,
    truth = Bullying,
    estimate = .pred_class,
    event_level = "second"
)
```

::: {.fragment}
> 🎯 With imbalanced outcomes, **don't trust accuracy alone**. Sensitivity and specificity tell the real story.
:::

In your `ml-template`, open **`models/knn.qmd`** and:

::: {.incremental}

:::

---

## Step 2 — Make KNN-friendly choices 🛠️

::: {.incremental}
4. Update the recipe:
   ```r
   step_downsample(<outcome>, under_ratio = 1) |>
   step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
   step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
   step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
   step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
   step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())
   ```
5. Swap the spec:
   ```r
   nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune()) |>
       set_engine("kknn") |>
       set_mode("classification")
   ```
:::

---

## Step 3 — Tune, sanity-check, last_fit 🚀

::: {.incremental}
6. Build the K grid (try `c(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 15, 21, 31, 51)`).
7. **CV sanity-check** with `fit_resamples()`.
8. `last_fit()` + confusion matrix + ROC.
9. **Render** your website. 🌐
